Two concurrent GETs can both retrieve the same existing one-time object before either deletion. This violates README `73` and the response's one-time claim. R2 strong consistency does not turn get-plus-later-delete into an atomic consume. Requires an existing one-time object (e.g. previously stored, separately seeded, or after B-P1 is repaired); this snapshot's failing upload path must not be ignored when describing end-to-end incidence. A lock/serialized claim design is needed for strict exclusivity; moving delete immediately after get narrows but does not eliminate the race.
- **B-A2, random-key collisions overwrite existing files:** keys consist of six `Math.random` base-36 characters (`532-538`) plus MIME-derived suffix (`383-397`), and `put` has no collision/precondition protection (`413-418`). Two same-extension uploads assigned the same ID overwrite the earlier object and metadata. Keyspace is 36^6 for each suffix; this is probabilistic, workload-dependent, and downstream of B-P1.
